#{Dynamically scale edge penalties via tour length dispersion and target strictly maximal utility edges using an adaptive floating-point tolerance to prevent over-penalization.}

import numpy as np

def update_edge_distance(edge_distance, local_opt_tour, edge_n_used):
    updated_edge_distance = np.copy(edge_distance)
    
    u_idx = local_opt_tour
    v_idx = np.roll(local_opt_tour, -1)
    
    tour_lengths = edge_distance[u_idx, v_idx]
    tour_counts = edge_n_used[u_idx, v_idx]
    
    utilities = tour_lengths / (1.0 + tour_counts)
    max_utility = np.max(utilities)
    
    # Restrict selection strictly to maximal-utility edges using machine epsilon tolerance
    atol = 1e-12 * (1.0 + np.abs(max_utility))
    selected_mask = utilities >= (max_utility - atol)
    
    # Scale penalty dynamically based on the spread (standard deviation) and average of tour edge lengths
    avg_edge = np.mean(tour_lengths)
    std_edge = np.std(tour_lengths)
    cv = std_edge / (avg_edge + 1e-12)
    dynamic_multiplier = np.clip(0.1 + 0.5 * cv, 0.1, 0.5)
    penalty = dynamic_multiplier * (avg_edge + std_edge)
    
    sel_u = u_idx[selected_mask]
    sel_v = v_idx[selected_mask]
    
    updated_edge_distance[sel_u, sel_v] += penalty
    updated_edge_distance[sel_v, sel_u] += penalty
    
    return updated_edge_distance
